options.C: On the back of the hand
options.D: In the antecubital fossa of the elbow

explanation: Exactly! The median cubital vein sits right across the bend of the elbow (the antecubital fossa), making it super accessible for quick IV lines and blood tests. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T6#GNS311_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which hormone tells the Leydig cells in the testes to produce testosterone?

options.A: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.B: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.C: Luteinizing hormone
options.D: Thyroid-stimulating hormone

explanation: Spot on! Luteinizing hormone (LH) comes from the anterior pituitary gland and travels down to tell the Leydig cells to make testosterone. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h1)

question: A patient is admitted with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis. What do you do right away?

options.A: Contact precautions
options.B: Droplet precautions
options.C: Standard precautions only
options.D: Airborne precautions

explanation: TB travels easily through tiny air particles. Setting up airborne precautions and grabbing an N95 protects everyone immediately. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h4)

question: How do many Nigerian families typically approach end-of-life decisions compared to Western models?

options.A: By leaving all choices entirely to junior hospital staff
options.B: Through a communal approach involving extended family members
options.C: By signing formal living wills upon hospital admission
options.D: By avoiding discussions about death and dying completely

explanation: In many Nigerian and African cultures, health decisions are rarely made alone. They are usually discussed and decided together as an extended family unit. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is a major reason why unsafe injections happen in low-resource clinics?

options.A: Having too many nurses on duty at night
options.B: Having way too many sterile water supplies
options.C: Shortages of disposable syringes and safety boxes
options.D: Too many mandatory infection control classes

explanation: When basic supplies run low, healthcare workers are put in tough spots. Advocating for proper supplies is a big part of nursing advocacy. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why are the testicles located outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To keep sperm production at a cooler temperature than body core temperature
options.B: To protect the delicate sperm cells from harsh digestive enzymes
options.C: To make it easier for the body to produce testosterone hormones
options.D: To increase the pressure needed for proper ejaculation

explanation: Sperm production requires a slightly cooler environment than internal body temperature to develop properly. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h2)

question: During early preeclampsia, what goes wrong with the blood vessels supplying the placenta?

options.A: They fail to widen and stay too narrow.
options.B: They wander completely away from the placenta.
options.C: They burst and cause heavy internal bleeding.
options.D: They multiply too fast and block blood flow.

explanation: Normally, these spiral arteries open up wide to feed the baby. When they stay tight and narrow, the placenta gets stressed from lack of blood flow, kicking off preeclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h2)

question: What does the medical acronym SUDEP stand for in epilepsy?

options.A: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy
options.B: Severe unprovoked disorder of electrical pathways
options.C: Spontaneous upper digestive episode pathology
options.D: Secondary unstable depression and epilepsy

explanation: SUDEP refers to the rare and tragic sudden death of a person with epilepsy where no other clear cause can be found. Keep up your steady study routine! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h8)

question: Which imaging test is best for checking a suspected torn knee ligament?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.B: Standard skeletal X-ray
options.C: Computed tomography scan
options.D: Traditional bone scan

explanation: MRI uses strong magnets to create super clear pictures of soft tissues like cartilage and ligaments, making it the top choice for soft tissue knee injuries. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h4)

question: If a mother has an umbilical cord prolapse, what position should you put her in right away?

options.A: Flat supine position with legs fully extended
options.B: Knee-chest or exaggerated Sims position
options.C: Left lateral position with head elevated high
options.D: Upright sitting position in a delivery chair

explanation: Gravity is key here! This position gets the baby's weight off the cord so oxygen can keep flowing while you prep for emergency help. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h8)

question: A woman who gets pregnant less than six months after her previous delivery is at higher risk for which complication?

options.A: Development of type 1 diabetes
options.B: Permanent loss of vision
options.C: Severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Early onset menopause

explanation: Closely spaced pregnancies strain the uterine muscles, increasing the likelihood of poor uterine contraction and heavy bleeding after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h1)

question: What does 'cohorting' mean in the ward?

options.A: Placing patients with the same infection in the same room
options.B: Training new nursing students in isolation procedures
options.C: Sharing medical equipment between different hospital wards
options.D: Moving a patient to a room with negative air pressure

explanation: When single rooms run out, grouping patients with the exact same infection together is a smart way to manage space and safety. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h6)

question: Which needle size and length is standard for an adult intramuscular injection?

options.A: 25 gauge, 1/2 inch needle
options.B: 27 gauge, 3/8 inch needle
options.C: 22 gauge, 1.5 inch needle
options.D: 31 gauge, 5/8 inch needle

explanation: You need a longer needle and a wider opening (like a 22-gauge, 1.5-inch) to bypass skin and fat and reach deep down into adult muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h3)

question: What does a rising serum lactate level usually mean for a sick patient?

options.A: Red blood cells are multiplying too quickly in the bone marrow
options.B: The patient is eating too many carbohydrates in their tube feeding
options.C: The kidneys are filtering waste products much faster than normal
options.D: Tissues are not getting enough oxygen and are using anaerobic metabolism

explanation: When cells are starved of oxygen, they switch to an emergency backup energy system that leaves behind lactic acid as waste. High lactate = cells need oxygen! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is a big clinical plus of using biphasic defibrillators over monophasic ones?

options.A: They automatically treat both shockable and non-shockable rhythms
options.B: They achieve success with lower energy levels and less tissue injury
options.C: They do not require any conductive gel pads on the chest
options.D: They can deliver shocks safely through wet clothing

explanation: Because biphasic shocks work so well, we don't need as much electricity. This keeps the patient safer by lowering the risk of skin burns and heart muscle damage. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h3)

question: If a patient loses their pulse, what document should you check right away to see if they didn't want life-saving efforts?

options.A: Patient admission summary
options.B: Do Not Resuscitate order
options.C: Daily nursing care plan
options.D: Discharge planning form

explanation: Great thinking! A DNR order tells the team whether the patient requested to skip measures like CPR. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the safety rules for giving medications?

options.A: Right patient identity
options.B: Right dosage amount
options.C: Right drug name
options.D: Right room decoration

explanation: Haha, room decor won't help your patient! We stick to the vital rights like right patient, drug, dose, route, and time. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T2#GNS125_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is high potassium (hyperkalemia) considered so dangerous to patient safety?

options.A: It melts the protective coating on nerves
options.B: It can cause fatal changes in heart rhythm
options.C: It causes severe bone fractures
options.D: It immediately stops the lungs from breathing

explanation: Potassium directly controls the electrical activity of the heart muscle, so high levels easily trigger lethal heart rhythms. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is cor pulmonale?

options.A: Infection of the heart valves resulting from severe pneumonia
options.B: Narrowing of the coronary arteries due to chronic low blood oxygen
options.C: Weakening of the left ventricle caused by systemic high blood pressure
options.D: Right heart failure caused by primary lung or pulmonary vascular disease

explanation: Spot on! Cor pulmonale happens when lung problems create high pressure in the pulmonary vessels, forcing the right side of the heart to struggle and eventually fail. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h6)

question: How do health ministries primarily use vital statistics data?

options.A: To test the speed of computer networks in wards
options.B: To decide which medications taste best
options.C: To allocate medical budgets and place facilities
options.D: To grade nursing students on final exams

explanation: Governments use population data to figure out where to spend money and build clinics based on real community needs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which gland releases cortisol when signaled by the pituitary gland during stress?

options.A: Adrenal cortex
options.B: Thyroid gland
options.C: Pineal gland
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: The outer layer of your adrenal glands (right above your kidneys) is called the adrenal cortex, and it pumps out cortisol to help you handle stress. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T8#GNS123_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the go-to medication used to stop and prevent seizures in severe pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Diazepam tablets
options.B: Oxytocin injection
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Paracetamol syrup

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is our absolute best friend for preventing and stopping eclamptic fits. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h4)

question: Why should a rehabilitation nurse avoid doing every single daily task for a patient?

options.A: It increases the risk of hospital-acquired infections
options.B: It stops the patient from regaining their independence
options.C: It violates standard medication administration policy
options.D: It causes immediate physical exhaustion for the nursing staff

explanation: Great nursing care means encouraging independence! If we do everything for our patients, they miss out on the practice they need to rebuild their strength. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h2)

question: A child keeps coming back to the clinic with severe diarrhea. What should you check first?

options.A: Assessing the family's source of drinking water and home sanitation
options.B: Telling the mother to stop feeding the child local home-cooked meals
options.C: Prescribing stronger antibiotics and keeping the child in the ward
options.D: Advising the parents to move to a different country entirely

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! Repeated diarrhea usually points to dirty water or poor home hygiene, so checking the root cause stops the cycle. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h7)

question: What major upper reproductive tract condition can happen if cervicitis is left untreated?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Endometriosis of the bowel
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)

explanation: If lower tract infections aren't cleared, they can creep upward and turn into pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h7)

question: What is the main danger of polycythemia vera (a condition where the body makes too many blood cells)?

options.A: Hyperviscosity and abnormal clot formation
options.B: Massive platelet destruction and bleeding
options.C: Severe iron deficiency and rapid hemolysis
options.D: Total bone marrow aplasia and infection

explanation: When you have too many cells packed into the blood, it gets thick and sludgy (hyperviscosity). This makes dangerous blood clots much more likely to form. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective clinical problem solving?

options.A: Fatigue and physical burnout
options.B: Heavy workloads and rushed decisions
options.C: Adequate staffing and clear communication
options.D: Fear of making mistakes and facing blame

explanation: Adequate staffing and clear communication help problem solving rather than acting as a barrier. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h5)

question: What tool do midwives use during labor to track contractions, dilation, and baby's heart rate on one sheet?

options.A: Temperature chart
options.B: Immunization card
options.C: Partograph
options.D: Admission register

explanation: You got it! The partograph is a nurse's best friend in the labor room for spotting trouble early and keeping track of progress. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h4)

question: During a family consultation, a mother yells at her teenage daughter for missing doses of her asthma inhaler. What is the nurse's best initial action?

options.A: Agree with the mother that the teenager is being irresponsible and lazy.
options.B: Intervene to calm the environment and encourage calm dialogue between them.
options.C: Ask the mother to leave the room permanently so she cannot return.
options.D: Give the teenager a stern warning about the dangers of severe asthma attacks.

explanation: Nurses must de-escalate tension and model constructive communication to help families work through conflicts safely. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h5)

question: Why is it important to conduct nursing research right here in Nigeria instead of relying only on foreign studies?

options.A: Local challenges like resource limits and culture differ from other regions
options.B: Foreign research studies are always fake and poorly written
options.C: Nigerian hospitals are not allowed to read international journals
options.D: International research never deals with patient care issues

explanation: You got it! Solutions have to fit our local Nigerian environment, culture, and available resources to actually work on our wards. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h7)

question: When cleaning the skin around a drainage tube, what is the correct direction to wipe?

options.A: Strictly from the bottom of the wound up toward the top
options.B: Back and forth rapidly across the entire wound surface
options.C: From the outer edges of the tape inward toward the tubing
options.D: In a circular motion starting at the tube and moving outward

explanation: Cleaning from the cleanest area (the insertion site) toward the dirtier outer skin prevents dragging outside bacteria closer to the wound opening. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h5)

question: What is the safest site for giving an intramuscular injection to an adult?

options.A: Dorsogluteal
options.B: Vastus lateralis
options.C: Deltoid
options.D: Ventrogluteal

explanation: You got it! The ventrogluteal site is clear of major nerves and blood vessels, making it the safest choice for adult IM injections. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T3#GNS122_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main job of glial cells in the nervous system?

options.A: To connect bone to bone across movable joints
options.B: To generate electrical impulses for muscle contraction
options.C: To support, protect, and nourish the neurons
options.D: To form a tough protective membrane around the brain

explanation: Think of glial cells as the supportive backup team—they take care of the neurons so the neurons can focus on sending signals! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h5)

question: Who is your go-to expert for tricky drug compatibility questions in the hospital?

options.A: The hospital accountant
options.B: The physical therapist
options.C: The facility security guard
options.D: The clinical pharmacist

explanation: Pharmacists are absolute masters of drug chemistry and interactions. Never hesitate to ask them for help! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T9#GNS125_U1_T9_h7)

question: Which tool is commonly used with a penlight to check the front part of the nose?

options.A: Ophthalmoscope
options.B: Nasal speculum
options.C: Laryngoscope
options.D: Tympanometer

explanation: A nasal speculum gently opens up the nostril so you can easily inspect the inside lining and nasal septum. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h4)

question: A young adult patient has lost a large amount of blood from a trauma, yet their blood pressure remains normal. What is the best explanation for this?

options.A: Young adults are immune to the effects of hypovolemic shock
options.B: The bleeding has completely stopped on its own
options.C: Strong blood vessel constriction is temporarily hiding the blood loss
options.D: The blood loss is minor and requires no further observation

explanation: Strong compensatory mechanisms in younger patients can keep blood pressure normal even after losing a dangerous amount of blood. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h3)

question: Which type of precaution requires the use of a negative-pressure room?

options.A: Droplet precautions
options.B: Airborne precautions
options.C: Standard precautions
options.D: Contact precautions

explanation: Airborne precautions require special negative-pressure ventilation to keep infectious particles from escaping into the hallway. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which ethical rule reminds nurses to make sure their actions cause no extra harm to a vulnerable patient?

options.A: Non-maleficence
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Justice

explanation: Non-maleficence simply means 'do no harm'. As nurses, protecting our patients from extra injury or distress is our core duty. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h2)

question: Which drug do we commonly use to boost weak contractions when there is no physical blockage?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Nifedipine
options.D: Dexamethasone

explanation: Brilliant! Oxytocin is our go-to medication because it mimics natural hormones to help the uterus contract more strongly. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h6)

question: Who acts as the central link for coordinating care between the patient and various medical specialists?

options.A: The nurse
options.B: The patient's family
options.C: The hospital accountant
options.D: The pharmacist

explanation: As the nurse, you are the heartbeat of the ward! You coordinate the care plan and make sure information flows smoothly between everyone involved. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h6)

question: What outdated myth sometimes stops providers from offering IUDs to young people?

options.A: The assumption that IUDs stop the user's heart from beating
options.B: The belief that IUDs are only safe for women who have children
options.C: The fear that IUDs permanently cure all forms of pelvic pain
options.D: The idea that IUDs require refrigeration before clinical insertion

explanation: Current clinical guidelines confirm that IUDs are safe and effective for adolescents, even if they haven't had children yet. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of prescribing symptomatic medications in degenerative conditions?

options.A: To improve patient comfort and daily functioning
options.B: To stop all future cell death in the brain
options.C: To completely cure the underlying chronic illness
options.D: To permanently reverse any genetic mutations

explanation: You nailed it! When a disease can't be cured yet, our nursing focus shifts to easing symptoms so the patient can stay comfortable and independent for as long as possible. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h3)

question: Which vaccines should nurses recommend to help protect patients against viral STIs and related long-term complications?

options.A: Tetanus and diphtheria
options.B: BCG and yellow fever
options.C: HPV and Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria and typhoid

explanation: Spot on! HPV and Hep B vaccines are powerful shields against major viral infections that can cause serious long-term issues like liver damage or cancers. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h8)

question: Which of these is a common nursing diagnosis for a patient with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Impaired Urinary Elimination from infection
options.B: Risk for Peripheral Neurovascular Dysfunction
options.C: Ineffective Airway Clearance
options.D: Risk for Unstable Blood Glucose Level

explanation: Exactly! When diabetes is uncontrolled, keeping blood sugar within a safe range is tough, making glucose instability the primary nursing focus. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T15#GNS222_U2_T15_h3)

question: How does a hiatus hernia make acid reflux worse?

options.A: It disrupts the closing ability of the lower sphincter
options.B: It blocks food from entering the small intestine
options.C: It inflames the lining of the large bowel
options.D: It causes the stomach to produce extra acid daily

explanation: When part of the stomach pushes up through the diaphragm, it messes with the natural pressure barrier that normally keeps food and acid safely locked in the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why does a midwife perform a gentle rectal exam after a delivery?

options.A: To evaluate the baseline tone of the pelvic floor muscles
options.B: To stimulate uterine contractions and prevent postpartum bleeding
options.C: To check if the anal sphincter and rectal mucosa are injured
options.D: To ensure the placenta has been completely expelled

explanation: It's a quick and necessary check to make sure a deep tear hasn't hidden itself by extending into the anal sphincter or rectal wall. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h4)

question: Which lab test is our best friend for spotting heart muscle damage?

options.A: Serum creatinine
options.B: Troponin
options.C: Serum potassium
options.D: White blood cell count

explanation: Troponin is a special protein found inside heart muscle. When the heart gets hurt, troponin leaks out into the bloodstream for us to spot on labs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why do we carefully control the speed at which the baby's head is born?

options.A: To ensure the placenta detaches immediately
options.B: To prevent the umbilical cord from snapping
options.C: To give the mother time to drink water
options.D: To prevent severe tearing of the perineum

explanation: Spot on! Guiding the head out slowly gives the perineal tissues time to stretch gently, preventing deep tears. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T006#GNS226_U3_T006_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT the right way to handle workplace violence in a hospital?

options.A: Using de-escalation techniques to calm an agitated patient
options.B: Ensuring an easy exit route is available during a patient interview
options.C: Accepting physical abuse quietly because it is part of the job
options.D: Reporting all threatening incidents to hospital security and management

explanation: Violence is never part of the job description. If someone threatens or abuses you, report it and use your hospital's security protocols immediately. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h6)

question: Why can a blood problem cause symptoms all over the body?

options.A: The lymphatic system traps blood proteins
options.B: Blood flows through every single organ system
options.C: Bone marrow is found in many bones
options.D: Blood cells change shape quickly in the air

explanation: Since blood travels everywhere in the body, when something is off with our blood components, it can show up as tiredness, weakness, or bruising anywhere. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of giving 'false reassurance' to a worried patient?

options.A: "Let us talk about what to expect during your recovery period."
options.B: "Everything is going to be completely fine, do not worry."
options.C: "Surgery carries risks, but your surgeon is very experienced."
options.D: "Tell me more about what is making you feel afraid today."

explanation: Telling someone 'everything will be fine' might sound nice, but it brushes off their real fears with an empty promise. It's better to listen and support them! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of secondary prevention, like routine screenings?

options.A: Stopping environmental toxins from entering the local community
options.B: Preventing healthy individuals from ever encountering risk factors
options.C: Restoring full physical strength after cancer treatment finishes
options.D: Detecting disease early when it is easiest and most successful to treat

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching things early through screening so you can tackle them before they grow into a bigger problem. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h3)

question: Which lab results must you check before a patient gets IV contrast dye for a CT scan?

options.A: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.B: Hemoglobin and hematocrit percentage
options.C: Serum potassium and sodium levels
options.D: White blood cell count and platelet level

explanation: Contrast dye is filtered by the kidneys. Checking kidney function tests like creatinine and BUN ensures the kidneys can safely handle the dye! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is the time right after breakfast often the best time to try having a bowel movement?

options.A: Stomach acid levels are at their lowest point of the day
options.B: Blood pressure peaks and helps push waste forward
options.C: Eating food triggers a natural wave of activity in the colon
options.D: Digestive enzymes are most active in the rectum then

explanation: Eating stimulates the gastrocolic reflex, which increases muscle contractions in the colon and creates a natural urge to go. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why do you need to check a patient's medication list before they get an EMG test?

options.A: To ensure the patient has taken their daily antibiotics
options.B: To prevent allergic reactions to the conductive gel used
options.C: To stop pain medications that would numb the skin entirely
options.D: To check for drugs that thin the blood and risk bleeding

explanation: Because an EMG involves placing thin needles directly into muscle tissue, taking blood thinners can put the patient at risk for internal bleeding or hematomas. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is it so important to figure out the exact type of prostatitis a patient has?

options.A: It indicates that immediate surgical removal of the prostate is needed
options.B: It prevents the future development of benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.C: It proves whether the patient has concurrent testicular cancer
options.D: It dictates whether antibiotics or non-infectious management is required

explanation: Brilliant! Bacterial infections need antibiotics, while other types of pelvic pain need a totally different, non-infectious treatment plan. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h3)

question: When does the general survey of a patient actually begin?

options.A: After listening to the patient's heart and lungs
options.B: When the blood pressure cuff is inflated
options.C: When writing the final discharge notes
options.D: The moment the nurse first sees the patient

explanation: The general survey starts immediately through observation before any hands-on examination takes place. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h4)

question: Which medication class is appropriate for a patient experiencing severe pain at Step 3 of the WHO analgesic ladder?

options.A: Strong opioids such as morphine
options.B: Skeletal muscle relaxants alone
options.C: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.D: Mild opioids such as codeine

explanation: Step 3 of the WHO ladder is designed for severe pain and utilizes strong opioids like morphine, fentanyl, or oxycodone. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h4)

question: A hospital director in Lagos wants to start primary nursing on a busy surgical ward. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ensure an adequate mix of registered staff and provide training on clinical autonomy.
options.B: Fire all doctors on the ward to give nurses complete control over the hospital.
options.C: Reduce the number of visiting hours to zero minutes per day.
options.D: Ban patients from asking questions about their medications.

explanation: To make primary nursing work, management must first ensure there are enough qualified nurses and empower them to make independent clinical decisions. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T3#GNS123_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of giving a daily bed bath to a very ill patient?

options.A: Providing gentle touch and comfort to the patient
options.B: Permanently curing chronic underlying heart disease
options.C: Removing sweat and bacteria from the skin surface
options.D: Allowing the nurse to inspect the skin for early redness

explanation: Bed baths are amazing for hygiene, comfort, and skin checks, but they unfortunately can't fix chronic internal conditions like heart disease. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation nursing compared to acute care?

options.A: Providing permanent custodial long-term institutional care
options.B: Stabilizing immediate life-threatening medical crises
options.C: Curing the underlying pathological disease process
options.D: Restoring the patient to their highest level of independence

explanation: You've got this! While acute care is all about surviving the emergency, rehab is here to help patients get back on their feet and do as much for themselves as possible. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h1)

question: What is the medical term for a fit?

options.A: Spasm
options.B: Stroke
options.C: Seizure
options.D: Syncope

explanation: A fit is medically referred to as a seizure, which involves abnormal electrical activity in the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h1)

question: You walk into the ward and notice the fridge storing insulin was unplugged all night. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Inject a test dose on a stable patient to verify potency.
options.B: Use the insulin immediately before it warms up further.
options.C: Quarantine the insulin and consult pharmacy before using it.
options.D: Discard the insulin quietly without logging the incident.

explanation: Safety first! Heat ruins insulin. Always isolate the suspect drugs and check with the pharmacy team rather than guessing if they are still good. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the main reason a doctor would order an EEG test?

options.A: Locating tumors in the spinal column
options.B: Diagnosing and evaluating seizure disorders
options.C: Detecting blockages in carotid arteries
options.D: Measuring pressure inside the eye chambers

explanation: EEGs are most commonly used to catch those tricky abnormal electrical patterns linked with epilepsy and seizures. Super important clinical tool! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which infection is a nurse most afraid of contracting after an accidental needle stick injury?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria

explanation: That's right! Blood-borne viruses like Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV are our biggest concerns after a sharp injury. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h6)

question: A nurse receives a fresh batch of IV antibiotics. Where should the nurse place them relative to the older stock already on the shelf?

options.A: Inside the nurse's personal locker
options.B: Behind the older stock
options.C: On a completely different floor
options.D: In front of the older stock

explanation: Placing new stock behind older stock ensures the older items are picked first, practicing FIFO and preventing expiration. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h3)

question: A young patient is worried that getting a contraceptive implant will make her permanently barren. How should you reassure her?

options.A: Confirm her fear and advise her to avoid all modern methods
options.B: Suggest she use ineffective traditional herbs instead
options.C: Ignore her concern and insert the device without discussion
options.D: Explain that fertility returns quickly once the implant is removed

explanation: You nailed it! Explaining that these methods are fully reversible helps calm her fears and builds strong trust. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h7)

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations falls under which level of prevention?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention stops diseases from occurring in the first place through measures like vaccination and health promotion. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which phase of cancer development involves a permanent change or mutation in a cell's DNA?

options.A: Initiation
options.B: Progression
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Promotion

explanation: You nailed it! Initiation is always step one—it's the very first moment a trigger causes a permanent genetic change in a normal cell. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why does a drop in estrogen after menopause put women at a higher risk for osteoporosis?

options.A: Estrogen is required to keep the surrounding skeletal muscles strong
options.B: Estrogen prevents the synovial membrane from producing enough fluid
options.C: Estrogen normally helps suppress osteoclast activity and supports bone building
options.D: Estrogen directly stops the kidneys from absorbing dietary vitamin D

explanation: Estrogen acts like a shield for bones by keeping bone-breaking cells (osteoclasts) under control. When it drops, bone breakdown speeds up. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T20#GNS222_U1_T20_h4)

question: What do we mean by an 'acute abdomen' in clinical practice?

options.A: Chronic indigestion caused by spicy food
options.B: Sudden, severe abdominal pain that often requires urgent surgery
options.C: A normal feeling of fullness after a large meal
options.D: A mild muscle cramp after heavy exercise

explanation: Spot on! An 'acute abdomen' is a red flag for sudden, severe belly pain that usually means trouble inside, like appendicitis or a perforation, needing quick surgical eyes. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main focus of embryology?

options.A: The analysis of genetic mutations during adult life
options.B: The microscopic examination of human bone tissue
options.C: The study of prenatal development from fertilization to birth
options.D: The physical changes that occur during normal aging

explanation: Embryology simply looks at how a new baby grows and develops inside the womb, right from the very first cell union up until birth. You've got this! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the main goal of doing a slit-lamp examination?

options.A: To wash out dust from the lower eyelid
options.B: To get a close-up, magnified view of the front of the eye
options.C: To measure exact distance vision
options.D: To check the patient's full side vision

explanation: The slit-lamp shines a bright, magnified light on front eye structures like the cornea, iris, and lens so you can see them clearly. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is 'compassion fatigue' in nursing?

options.A: Physical muscle tiredness from standing too long during a shift
options.B: Emotional exhaustion and decreased empathy from continuous exposure to patient suffering
options.C: Boredom caused by doing administrative paperwork all day
options.D: A temporary lack of sleep after working a single night shift

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when nurses absorb ongoing patient trauma without enough time to recharge, leaving them feeling emotionally drained. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h8)

question: A client expresses fear that a contraceptive injection will cause permanent infertility based on rumors heard in the market. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Provide accurate, gentle education and explain how the method temporarily works
options.B: Agree with the rumor to prevent any future arguments
options.C: Refuse to provide any family planning services to this client
options.D: Scold the client for listening to uneducated people in the community

explanation: Nurses must address fears and correct misconceptions with patience and clear scientific facts rather than judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h6)

question: Why do fungal infections of the toenails (onychomycosis) usually need oral pills instead of just a surface cream?

options.A: Topical creams cannot penetrate deeply enough through the hard nail plate
options.B: Fungi living in toenails are completely immune to all topical antifungal creams
options.C: Topical medications wash away too quickly from the foot due to sweat
options.D: Nail infections are always caused by systemic internal organ failure

explanation: Correct! The nail plate is thick and tough, acting like a shield that surface creams can't pass through. Pills are needed to reach the fungus from within. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h4)

question: Why do nurses need to understand how different imaging tests work?

options.A: To operate the heavy imaging machinery during off-peak night shifts
options.B: To independently prescribe the exact type of scan a patient needs in an emergency
options.C: To safely coordinate studies, prepare patients, and guide nursing care based on results
options.D: To replace the radiologist in reading detailed cross-sectional scans

explanation: You won't be running the big scanner machines yourself, but knowing how each test works helps you prep your patient and understand what the results mean for their care! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the main job of a healthy fallopian tube?

options.A: To filter waste products from the pelvic cavity
options.B: To provide a pathway for the egg and the site for fertilization
options.C: To produce female hormones like estrogen and progesterone
options.D: To nourish the developing embryo throughout the entire pregnancy

explanation: Think of the fallopian tube as the highway where the egg travels and meets sperm for fertilization. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T28#GNS216_U5_T28_h1)

question: A patient with a degenerative condition frequently becomes exhausted halfway through a morning walk. What physical therapy strategy should be introduced?

options.A: Energy conservation and activity pacing
options.B: Complete bed rest to eliminate all physical exertion
options.C: Immediate removal of all walking aids
options.D: High-intensity weight lifting to build sudden bulk

explanation: Teaching the patient to pace themselves and conserve energy helps them stay active without burning out all their strength at once. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h4)

question: What complication is a patient most at risk for if they receive many blood transfusions over several years?

options.A: Acute hemolytic shock
options.B: Immediate anaphylaxis
options.C: Bacterial sepsis
options.D: Iron overload

explanation: Our bodies are great at using iron, but terrible at getting rid of excess iron! Over years of multiple transfusions, that extra iron starts piling up in vital organs like the liver and heart. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T12#GNS311_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why is retraining better than punishing staff when errors pop up in data collection?

options.A: Staff members prefer being disciplined over learning new skills
options.B: Retraining is always cheaper than buying new paper forms
options.C: Punitive measures violate international supply chain laws
options.D: Punishment encourages staff to hide mistakes rather than fix them

explanation: You got it! When people are terrified of punishment, they fake records to look flawless, which ruins the reliability of our health data. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h7)

question: Which condition is classically associated with a "bird-beak" tapering appearance at the bottom of the esophagus?

options.A: Zenker's diverticulum
options.B: Hiatal hernia
options.C: Gastric ulcer
options.D: Achalasia

explanation: Achalasia prevents the lower esophageal sphincter from opening properly, creating a narrow, bird-beak shape on the X-ray film as barium tries to pass. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h6)

question: What do we call a sudden, severe change in mental state where a patient becomes very confused and restless?

options.A: Chronic anemia
options.B: Stable hypertension
options.C: Mild osteoarthritis
options.D: Acute delirium

explanation: Delirium is a sudden, temporary state of confusion often seen in hospitalised patients. It puts them at risk of pulling out their IV lines or climbing out of bed unassisted. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h4)

question: A patient shows signs of severe perinatal depression with thoughts of self-harm. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Telling her to snap out of it because motherhood is joyful
options.B: Facilitating an immediate referral to a mental health specialist
options.C: Suggesting she avoid speaking with her partner about it
options.D: Waiting until the postpartum checkup to mention it

explanation: Safety first! Severe mental health red flags always require urgent professional care and specialist support. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T004#GNS226_U2_T004_h8)

question: Which factor actually helps lower a woman's chances of getting epithelial ovarian cancer?

options.A: A woman who used oral contraceptive pills for over five years
options.B: A woman with a strong family history of breast cancer
options.C: A woman who underwent early menarche and late menopause
options.D: A nulliparous woman of advanced maternal age

explanation: You got it! Anything that pauses ovulation—like birth control pills, pregnancy, or breastfeeding—gives the ovaries a break and lowers cancer risk. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h3)

question: Why does wearing the correct glove size matter so much in clinical work?

options.A: It prevents tearing and keeps your fingers nimble
options.B: It stops the material from causing latex allergies
options.C: It keeps the gloves completely sterile
options.D: It means you don't have to wash your hands afterwards

explanation: Gloves that are too tight will easily rip, while oversized gloves make it hard to grip things. Finding your right size is key! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h5)

question: How might a depressed older adult unusually show their emotional pain?

options.A: By writing poetry about deep emotional sorrow
options.B: By expressing intense excitement about the future
options.C: Through vague physical aches and sleep problems
options.D: Through sudden bursts of aggressive athletic activity

explanation: Older adults often express sadness through bodily aches and trouble sleeping rather than saying 'I feel depressed.' Good to know! [learn more](GNS321_U3_T3#GNS321_U3_T3_h4)

question: What type of water is best for soaking Plaster of Paris bandages?

options.A: Ice cold water
options.B: Boiling hot water
options.C: Carbonated water
options.D: Lukewarm water

explanation: Lukewarm water gives you a predictable setting time. Hot water makes it set way too fast, and cold water slows it right down. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the cerebellum?

options.A: Regulating basic breathing and heart rate
options.B: Processing conscious thought and reasoning
options.C: Producing cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: Coordinating balance and smooth body movements

explanation: The cerebellum fine-tunes motor activity and helps maintain posture and balance during movement. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main job of an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) during a cardiac arrest?

options.A: Provide mechanical chest compressions at a steady rate
options.B: Pump oxygen directly into the lungs of the patient
options.C: Measure the exact blood pressure of an unresponsive person
options.D: Deliver an electrical shock to reset an abnormal heart rhythm

explanation: Think of an AED as a smart device that checks the heart rhythm and gives a quick shock only when needed to get the heart beating right again. You've got this! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the term for right-sided heart failure caused by long-term lung disease?

options.A: Cor pulmonale
options.B: Myocardial infarction
options.C: Rheumatic carditis
options.D: Infective endocarditis

explanation: Cor pulmonale refers to enlargement and failure of the right ventricle resulting from high blood pressure in the pulmonary blood vessels due to lung disease. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h7)

question: In the theatre team, who is mainly responsible for writing down the counts on the whiteboard?

options.A: The lead surgeon
options.B: The scrub nurse
options.C: The anesthetist
options.D: The circulating nurse

explanation: The circulating nurse is outside the sterile field (unsterile zone), which makes them the perfect person to maintain the official tally board. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h3)

question: A patient has had lingering joint swelling for over eight months. What type of inflammation is this?

options.A: Chronic inflammation
options.B: Vascular collapse
options.C: Systemic sepsis
options.D: Acute inflammation

explanation: You got it! When inflammation hangs around for months with continuous immune activity, we call it chronic. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h2)

question: A patient is admitted with a skin infection spread by direct touch. Which nursing action is most important?

options.A: Placing the patient in a negative pressure isolation room
options.B: Putting on gloves and a gown before touching the patient's skin
options.C: Spraying the hallway air with strong chemical disinfectants
options.D: Boiling all eating utensils before the patient uses them

explanation: Because direct contact involves skin-to-skin touch or touching infected lesions, barriers like gloves and gowns block the transfer of pathogens. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which of these is a clear example of vector-borne transmission?

options.A: A person drinking contaminated well water
options.B: Inhaling droplets from a patient's cough
options.C: Direct skin contact with scabies mites
options.D: A mosquito spreading the malaria parasite

explanation: You got it! Vectors are living carriers like mosquitoes that pick up a germ and deliver it to a human host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T13#GNS313_U1_T13_h3)

question: Why is gentle hand expression of milk recommended before feeding when a mother's breasts are very swollen (engorged)?

options.A: It softens the areola so the infant can achieve a proper latch
options.B: It replaces the need for any future breastfeeding sessions
options.C: It cures underlying bacterial infections instantly
options.D: It permanently stops milk production in the affected breast

explanation: Severe swelling pulls the nipple flat, making it tricky for the baby to grip. Expressing a little milk first creates a softer surface to grasp. Well done! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h2)

question: When should you avoid doing passive range of motion exercises on a limb?

options.A: When the client has a fresh, unhealed bone fracture
options.B: When the ward weather is unusually warm
options.C: When the client has a mild cold
options.D: When the client feels sleepy in the afternoon

explanation: Spot on! Moving a limb with a fresh fracture disrupts bone healing and causes severe pain. Always check for fractures first! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main use of a partograph during labor?

options.A: To monitor labor progress and detect prolonged labor early
options.B: To measure the mother's daily nutritional intake
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of the hospital stay
options.D: To record the baby's immunization schedule after birth

explanation: The partograph is a midwife's best friend! It gives a clear picture of how labor is going so you can spot trouble early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h4)

question: What is the medical term for difficulty swallowing, which is common in some older adults?

options.A: Dyspnea
options.B: Dyspepsia
options.C: Dysphagia
options.D: Dysphasia

explanation: Correct! 'Dysphagia' means trouble swallowing. As nurses, keeping an eye on this helps us protect our older patients from choking. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T7#GNS324_U6_T7_h3)

question: When do doctors usually order tests for a patient with flatulence?

options.A: Only when the patient requests surgery to cure the problem
options.B: Before taking any dietary or lifestyle history from the patient
options.C: When warning signs like weight loss or rectal bleeding are present
options.D: Every time a patient reports passing gas more than five times a day

explanation: Regular gas doesn't need fancy tests, but red flags like bleeding mean we need to check deeper to keep our patients safe. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why is it so important to separate general rubbish from hazardous waste right when you throw it away?

options.A: To reduce the overall weight of general waste bins
options.B: To make it easier for administrative staff to empty trash cans
options.C: To prevent clean items from becoming dangerous and costly to treat
options.D: To comply with building design codes for hospitals

explanation: You got it! If you mix regular trash with infectious waste, the whole batch becomes contaminated. That drives up the volume—and the cost—of special waste disposal drastically. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a serious warning sign covered by the ACHES mnemonic?

options.A: Severe pain and swelling in the lower leg
options.B: Mild morning nausea and mild breast tenderness
options.C: Severe chest pain and shortness of breath
options.D: Sudden severe headaches with visual disturbances

explanation: Mild nausea and tender breasts are normal, everyday side effects when starting hormones. ACHES is meant to catch the rare, serious red flags! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T011#GNS226_U6_T011_h6)

question: Why do older adults get skin tears and pressure sores so easily?

options.A: Increased sweat gland production softens the skin too much
options.B: Rapid regeneration of skin cells creates a fragile top layer
options.C: High collagen production makes the skin stiff and brittle
options.D: Thinning of the epidermis and loss of subcutaneous fat

explanation: Elderly skin loses its natural padding (fat layer) and outer protection, making it delicate like tissue paper. Gentle handling is key! [learn more](GNS321_U3_T5#GNS321_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which feature is most essential for a successful adolescent reproductive health clinic?

options.A: Charging high fees to discourage casual visits by teenagers
options.B: Youth-friendly services with strict privacy and non-judgmental staff
options.C: Mandatory reporting of all adolescent clinic visitors to their parents
options.D: Locating the clinic inside high school classrooms during lessons

explanation: Adolescents avoid health facilities if they fear moral judgment or lack of confidentiality from staff. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of cancer screening programs?

options.A: To replace traditional biopsy procedures entirely
options.B: To detect cancer or precancerous changes early
options.C: To cure late-stage metastatic disease completely
options.D: To measure the exact cost of hospital stays

explanation: Screening aims to identify disease before symptoms appear so treatment can start when it is most effective. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a golden rule when suctioning airway secretions in a client with high ICP?

options.A: Turn the client flat on their back before starting suction
options.B: Skip pre-oxygenation to save time during the procedure
options.C: Avoid prolonged suctioning because coughing spikes ICP
options.D: Always suction for at least two full minutes to clear all mucus

explanation: Suctioning makes anyone cough and gag, which temporarily shoots up the pressure inside the head. Always keep your passes short and give oxygen first! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h6)

question: During an upper limb check, which finding means you need to report to the doctor right away?

options.A: Warm and pink nail beds
options.B: Normal breathing rate and rhythm
options.C: Strong grip strength in both hands
options.D: New numbness or tingling in the fingers

explanation: Numbness and tingling are red flags! They tell you a nerve might be pinched or irritated and needs urgent attention. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why might a client with a true seizure disorder still have a completely normal EEG result?

options.A: The electrodes were placed on the wrong side of the forehead
options.B: Abnormal electrical activity may not happen during the recording period
options.C: The recording machine can only detect slow wave patterns
options.D: Anticonvulsant medications permanently cure abnormal brain waves

explanation: An EEG is just a snapshot in time. A patient can have epilepsy and still have a totally quiet, normal EEG when the machine happens to be recording! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a good public health strategy for preventing birth defects?

options.A: Encouraging the use of unregulated herbal mixtures during pregnancy
options.B: Promoting rubella vaccinations
options.C: Ensuring women attend regular antenatal care
options.D: Educating communities about the risks of close-relative marriages

explanation: Spot on! Unregulated herbal concoctions can carry hidden teratogens that harm the developing baby, so we definitely don't recommend them. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h10)

question: What is the usual long-term outlook for children who get Acute Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Poor, with guaranteed progression to failure
options.B: Moderate, leading to chronic heart disease
options.C: Excellent, with most making a full recovery
options.D: Unpredictable, with lifelong dialysis needed

explanation: Unlike adults, kids with AGN almost always bounce back completely with the right care and rest. Such a relief to know for young patients and their families! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h9)

question: What is the main goal of taking anti-seizure medications?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any future medical follow-ups
options.B: Curing the underlying genetic mutation permanently
options.C: Inducing deep sedation to prevent all physical activity
options.D: Achieving complete seizure control with minimal side effects

explanation: Anti-seizure drugs aim to stop abnormal brain waves so the patient can live a normal, seizure-free life without feeling heavily drugged. Keep up the brilliant study habit! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h5)

question: What does viewing a patient in their social context primarily involve?

options.A: Isolating the patient from family members during treatment
options.B: Recognizing how relationships and living conditions affect health
options.C: Focusing strictly on the diseased organ and laboratory values
options.D: Prioritizing hospital policies over community traditions

explanation: Social context looks at the broader picture of a person's life, including family and living conditions, which deeply influence health outcomes. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: How do negative staff attitudes in hospitals affect male involvement?

options.A: They motivate men to build private clinics.
options.B: They discourage men from returning to the clinic.
options.C: They have no real effect on attendance rates.
options.D: They force men to study nursing on their own.

explanation: When nurses act unfriendly or unwelcoming, men feel unwanted and prefer to stay away next time. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T7#GNS312_U4_T7_h3)

question: What do most cases of colorectal cancer start from?

options.A: Chronic twisting of the sigmoid colon
options.B: Enlarged external hemorrhoids near the anus
options.C: Severe bacterial infections in the appendix
options.D: Benign polyps on the inner lining of the colon

explanation: Spot on! Most colorectal cancers start out as harmless growths called adenomatous polyps that slowly change over many years. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is strongly linked to developing primary bone cancer later in life?

options.A: Prior exposure to therapeutic ionizing radiation
options.B: Long-term bacterial infections of the joint space
options.C: Chronic dietary deficiency of calcium and vitamin D
options.D: High impact sports injuries during childhood

explanation: Previous radiation treatment for childhood cancers can unfortunately increase the risk of a secondary bone sarcoma down the road. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T19#GNS222_U1_T19_h2)

question: A patient on a strong psychiatric medication suddenly gets severe muscle stiffness and spasms. What drug class will the doctor most likely order?

options.A: Short-acting insulins
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Intravenous anticoagulants
options.D: Central anticholinergics

explanation: Brilliant! Anticholinergics are the go-to treatment for those pesky extrapyramidal side effects (muscle spasms and stiffness) caused by some antipsychotic drugs. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h4)

question: What does the clinical term 'paroxysmal' mean?

options.A: A permanent and irreversible nerve damage
options.B: A localized infection of the brain tissue
options.C: A sudden, unexpected, and temporary episode
options.D: A slow and progressive worsening of symptoms

explanation: You'll often hear 'paroxysmal' in the wards! It just means a sudden symptom flare-up that hits quickly, doesn't last forever, and then passes. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h1)

question: What does 'role reversal' mean for a child affected by HIV in the family?

options.A: The child takes on adult caregiving and household responsibilities
options.B: The community rejects the child and adopts the parents instead
options.C: The child stops going to school to teach younger children
options.D: The child becomes the legal guardian of the extended family

explanation: Role reversal happens when a young child has to nurse sick adults or care for younger siblings, missing out on their own childhood. Spotting this helps nurses offer better support! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is a major difference between vitamins and macronutrients like carbs and fats?

options.A: Vitamins are only used to build bones.
options.B: Vitamins are needed in much larger amounts.
options.C: Vitamins cannot be found in natural foods.
options.D: Vitamins do not supply calories.

explanation: Vitamins are vital for health, but unlike carbs, fats, and proteins, they don't give us energy or calories. They have other super important jobs! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T006#GNS227_U1_T006_h4)

question: What heavily shapes how a person expresses grief and mourning?

options.A: The specific brand of hospital bed
options.B: Culture and spiritual beliefs
options.C: The room number in the hospital
options.D: The time of day the patient was admitted

explanation: Spot on! Cultural background and spiritual worldview guide the rituals and social rules for how a community handles loss. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h7)

question: What is one of the biggest dangers of leaving a patient in a wet or soiled adult diaper for too long?

options.A: Permanent kidney failure
options.B: Skin breakdown and pressure injury
options.C: Chronic high blood pressure
options.D: Sudden loss of upper body strength

explanation: Moisture and waste trap heat and wetness against the skin, breaking down its defenses fast. Keeping patients clean and dry is one of your core superpowers as a nurse! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h4)

question: Which vitamin does the liver desperately need to build several key clotting factors?

question: Why is it vital for a nurse to spend time interviewing a young female patient alone during a clinic check-up?

question: Why do teenagers sometimes take big risks without fully thinking things through?

question: Biological sex is primarily determined by which of the following?

question: A patient drinks a mug of tea, receives an IV antibiotic piggyback, and eats a plate of rice. What counts as fluid intake?

question: What is the biggest danger when someone has a severe case of watery diarrhoea?

question: What are you trying to find out when you perform Leopold's maneuvers on a pregnant client?

question: What is the main purpose of an advanced healthcare directive?

question: Why must you always teach patients never to stop taking their antipsychotic medications abruptly on their own?

question: What is the medical word for bone marrow slowing down due to chemotherapy?

question: Why does urine output drop so much during cardiogenic shock?

question: Which sign tells you a newborn has latched on correctly for breastfeeding?

question: Why is an injury to the lower brain stem considered an immediate medical emergency?

question: When exercising the lower limbs, where should you place your hands to support the leg?

question: Why is hormone therapy often used to treat prostate cancer?

question: Why do hospital system issues often lead nurses to break safety rules?

question: How do anticoagulant medications help treat a deep vein thrombosis?
